## What it is

A monorepo where several ML systems share one substrate — data contracts,
features, evaluation, orchestration, serving, observability, governance and
agentic tooling — and each system is a **vertical** under `projects/`. The
projects differ in **kind** (time series, retrieval, agents), not merely in
dataset, because a substrate that serves one shape of problem has not been
shown to be a substrate. Multi-cloud by design (GCP and AWS), with every
non-trivial decision recorded as an ADR.

Its central claim is falsifiable and tested: *a second project reuses at least
three shared libraries with no fork* ([ADR-000](docs/decisions/ADR-000-charter-and-scope.md),
criterion C1, checked by `scripts/check_library_reuse.py`). If that fails, this
is a monorepo of unrelated projects.

**For** teams that run more than one ML system and want them to share what
should be shared — and adopters who want a worked example of governed MLOps
across kinds. **Not for** a single tabular service on Kubernetes: that is
[ml-service-template](https://github.com/DuqueOM/ml-service-template), smaller
and readable in an afternoon, which this repository consumes for its serving
layer ([ADR-003](docs/decisions/ADR-003-service-template-consumption.md))
rather than replacing. [docs/ADOPTION.md](docs/ADOPTION.md) is the full
decision guide.

## Quick start

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/DuqueOM/ml-platform.git    # the development line
cd ml-platform
bash scripts/bootstrap.sh                          # uv, the pinned Python, the locked workspace
uv run pytest projects/demand-forecast -q          # one vertical's suite
uv run copier copy --vcs-ref HEAD --trust . projects/my-project   # a vertical, with the locked Copier
```

`make verify` then runs every gate CI runs, on your machine.
[QUICK_START.md](QUICK_START.md) continues to a pod answering on a local kind
cluster (needs Docker); [docs/PROGRESSION.md](docs/PROGRESSION.md) takes it
from there to a second vertical and to a cloud.

## What you get

| Capability | Where it is, and what shows it is real |
| --- | --- |
| **Shared libraries** — conformal prediction, data contracts, point-in-time features, retrieval evaluation | `libs/`; a test fails any import that points upward ([ADR-001](docs/decisions/ADR-001-monorepo-topology.md)), and the reuse gate fails a fork |
| **Projects of different kinds** — demand forecasting on an Iceberg lakehouse, retrieval-augmented generation on pgvector, an agent with a deterministic policy gate | [`projects/`](projects/README.md), each with its README; demand-forecast and store-assistant also carry evaluation gates and a model card — rag-assistant's are recorded deviations from the [project contract](docs/PROJECT_CONTRACT.md) (P6, P7) |
| **A project generator** whose vertical meets six of the seven contract requirements as generated — the seventh, its evaluation thresholds, is left `TODO` for the adopter to decide | `templates/project/` (Copier); [docs/PROJECT_CONTRACT.md](docs/PROJECT_CONTRACT.md), checked by `tests/test_project_contract.py` |
| **Orchestration** — Airflow for the business flow, KFP for ML compute, judging promotion by one shared rule | [`orchestration/dags`](orchestration/dags/README.md), [`orchestration/pipelines`](orchestration/pipelines/README.md); `tests/test_promotion_agreement.py` |
| **Serving** from a scaffold generated by ml-service-template, with the model artifact loaded under the image's own requirements in CI | `services/`; gate P18 in [quality gates](docs/governance/quality-gates.md); [ADR-008](docs/decisions/ADR-008-serving-a-forecast-from-a-classification-scaffold.md) |
| **Infrastructure as code** — Terraform for GCP and AWS, Kustomize overlays per cloud and environment, an ArgoCD ApplicationSet, default-deny NetworkPolicies | [`platform/`](platform/kubernetes/README.md); rendered and tested in CI, never applied to a cloud — see the status above |
| **A local stack** on kind — Postgres with pgvector, an S3-compatible store, OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, Prometheus, Grafana | [platform/local/README.md](platform/local/README.md); `make local-up`, `make local-verify` |
| **Supply chain and security** — gitleaks over the full history, Trivy over the whole lock and over the serving image's resolved requirements (no image is built, so none is scanned), Bandit, commit-pinned actions, scanner baselines with owners and expiry | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [`.security-baselines/`](.security-baselines/README.md) |
| **Agentic governance** — one canonical set of rules, skills and workflows, rendered for Claude, Cursor, Codex and Devin, under an AUTO / CONSULT / STOP protocol | [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [ADR-005](docs/decisions/ADR-005-agentic-governance.md) |

## Architecture

```text
libs/            ml-core · data-contracts · feature-defs · llm-core · serving-core
projects/        one deployable ML system each, generated from templates/project/
orchestration/   Airflow DAGs + KFP pipelines
services/        serving, generated from ml-service-template (not edited here)
platform/        terraform · kubernetes · gitops · policies · observability · local
agentic/         rules · skills · workflows (canonical; per-tool files are pointers)
docs/            decisions · architecture · governance · datasets · runbooks
tests/           repository-level invariants
```

Dependencies point one way: `libs/` never imports `projects/`, and projects
never import each other — enforced by a test, not by review
([ADR-001](docs/decisions/ADR-001-monorepo-topology.md)). The
[technical plan](docs/architecture/technical-plan.md) gives each phase its
executable acceptance criteria; the [decisions index](docs/decisions/README.md)
lists every ADR with the alternatives it rejected.

## How claims are verified

- **Every published quality claim maps to a command that can fail a build.** A
  metric that is reported but cannot fail is decoration.
  [Quality gates](docs/governance/quality-gates.md) is that mapping, and a gate
  checks it for gaps.
- **Each claim carries the layer its evidence reaches** — L1 contract (tests),
  L2 component (the thing executed), L3 cluster (kind), L4 cloud. The layer is
  derived from the command that ran, never declared:
  [implementation status](docs/architecture/implementation-status.md).
- **An independent audit, enforced by CI.** QA-4 is run in a separate session
  against a fixed commit; when too many commits land after it, the
  documentation gate fails until the next one is recorded. The
  [procedure](docs/governance/qa-procedures.md#qa-4--independent-audit-auto-within-its-session), the reports under
  `docs/governance/qa4/`, and the [remediation work order](docs/governance/remediation-work-order.md).
- **Gates are watched failing.** A mutation catalogue (`tests/mutations.yaml`)
  breaks every implemented gate in [quality gates](docs/governance/quality-gates.md)
  on purpose and expects it to go red; a test fails an implemented gate that
  no entry breaks.
- **Measurements carry their method, and wrong claims are corrected in place
  with a date** rather than edited away.
